content.text: Why do we always see the same side of the Moon? It is tidally locked: it spins once for every trip around Earth, so the same face points our way, give or take a slight wobble called libration. The Moon phases only change how much of that face is lit. Photo: NASA, the full Moon over Kennedy Space Center.

socialAccounts.title: Same side of the Moon: why we always see it, and tidal locking
